source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Check version of BMC/BIOS from BIOS
2. Send command to check version of BMC : ipmitool raw 0x30 0x20

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Command should be sent successfully
2. Versions should be shown correctly before and after flashing.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" mc info 2>&1; echo ---; curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X GET https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory | jq .FirmwareInventory[].Name
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return BMC info + Redfish FirmwareInventory names and look for the DCSCM-CPLD entry. No RISK.

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES; assumes a Redfish collection shape and lists only names, so it neither proves a DCSCM-CPLD version nor preserves member-level evidence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / IMPROVED; fixes discovery, secrets and version-field evidence, but assumes project mapping alone may replace the contradictory Master operation.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 739/2291 accepts the DeepSeek command without resolving DCSCM-CPLD versus BMC/BIOS semantics.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its FULLY AUTOMATABLE conclusion is non-counting history; it records the source conflict but treats an undefined replacement procedure as an ordinary input.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves Master source, ED-36 permits BLOCKED for irreducible target/core-operation conflicts, ED-38 keeps verdict ownership with engineers and ED-39 prohibits firmware-target substitution.

original_test_intent: The Items request verification of the DCSCM-CPLD firmware version before and after a separate approved flash, while the preserved procedure never identifies DCSCM-CPLD or reads its version.
original_method: The Master observes BMC/BIOS versions and issues raw BMC command `0x30 0x20`. DeepSeek adds generic BMC information plus a Redfish inventory name list, but no component-bound version property.
manual_activity: An engineer must first decide whether this record is a DCSCM-CPLD version test or the copied BMC/BIOS test and approve the authoritative DCSCM-CPLD member and version property if the title remains controlling.
required_inputs: engineer decision on DCSCM-CPLD versus BMC/BIOS purpose
exact DCSCM-CPLD instance and component identity
advertised read-only inventory resource and canonical version property
expected before/after versions and related flash transaction
trusted BMC authentication and TLS policy
safety_requirements: Use no UpdateService POST/PATCH, image upload, reset, activation or undocumented raw command in this version-review testcase.
Do not treat HTTP success, an inventory member name or BMC `mc info` as proof of DCSCM-CPLD firmware version.
Do not use `curl -k`, literal credentials or credentials in logged command lines; require approved secrets and certificate validation.
Preserve full discovery, collection and member JSON once an authoritative mapping is approved.
Stop on missing or ambiguous component/version fields without retrying, guessing a schema or changing state.
agent_execution_scope: No execution while the Master target/core-operation contradiction remains unresolved.
After engineering approval, perform read-only service discovery, retrieve the exact DCSCM-CPLD member and compare its canonical version to the approved matrix.
Collect health and audit evidence without assigning the final DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Resolve whether DCSCM-CPLD is the authoritative target and approve the corresponding version-read procedure.
Approve the exact member identity, version property, expected before/after pair and equivalence of any Project Override.
Judge the final PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED result from valid evidence.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The assumed `/FirmwareInventory` array expression is not demonstrated by service discovery, `.Name` is not a version, `mc info` is BMC context and insecure TLS/credential handling is unacceptable.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: None until the target is resolved; afterward discover the advertised collection with trusted TLS, retain full payloads and extract only the engineer-approved DCSCM-CPLD member/version field.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: DCSCM-CPLD Items, copied BMC/BIOS wording, raw `0x30 0x20`, before/after Criteria, script and 5/0-minute values remain unchanged source evidence.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Resolve the source purpose; if DCSCM-CPLD is confirmed, use authenticated read-only service discovery or documented vendor inventory to bind an exact component member and canonical firmware version, then compare complete before/after evidence.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the platform whose DCSCM-CPLD inventory mapping is approved.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC, Redfish schema, client, DCSCM-CPLD and decoder revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform component inventory and vendor DCSCM-CPLD firmware-inventory specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Introduces the missing DCSCM-CPLD-specific read as a recommendation without altering the preserved BMC/BIOS source procedure.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A member name or BMC version cannot satisfy DCSCM-CPLD version coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Engineer purpose decision, component/property mapping and expected values.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Inventory paths and names may change; an unbound match could select the wrong CPLD or omit the version entirely.

project_override_considerations: After engineering resolves the target, Project SPEC may approve Redfish, IPMI or vendor tooling only if it identifies the same DCSCM-CPLD and canonical version. It must record the preserved source method, replacement reason, equivalent coverage and any original path left unverified.
expected_evidence: engineer-approved test purpose and exact DCSCM-CPLD identity
trusted service discovery and complete collection/member payloads
canonical version field with tool/schema metadata
approved before/after expected matrix and flash/activation reference
BMC/SEL/host health evidence and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items name DCSCM-CPLD, but the Master Procedure is explicitly BMC/BIOS and provides neither a DCSCM-CPLD selector nor a component-version field. The generic Criteria do not establish which version must match.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The blocker is a target/core-operation contradiction in the Master, not merely absent credentials or Project SPEC. A package cannot determine whether the copied BMC/BIOS operation should be retained or replaced; engineering must approve the intended component and valid read semantics first.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes YES to BLOCKED because name-only inventory and BMC context cannot prove the requested CPLD version and the transport weakens TLS/secret safety.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keeps its discovery and evidence safeguards but changes confirmation-gated to BLOCKED until engineering resolves the preserved source's target mismatch.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Rejects FULLY AUTOMATABLE because automating a hypothetical component mapping would silently replace the Master core operation before approval.

review_improvement: Prevents an inventory-name match from being promoted to version evidence and makes the DCSCM-CPLD versus BMC/BIOS design decision explicit.
independent_technical_reasoning: Read-only Redfish inventory can automate a DCSCM-CPLD version comparison only when a supported resource and canonical property are tied to the exact component. The source currently specifies different BMC/BIOS operations, while DeepSeek returns only names. Because neither path satisfies the named target and selecting a replacement requires engineering ownership, the static review is BLOCKED without claiming any DUT result.
